body:
Obiwan, you're right, I think I'd better read over the Manifesto more closely.
 I think lawnmowers deserve special scrutiny by the antitech groups because
not only do they create a lot of stressful noise, but they are used to mow
grass, and that kind of grass is nothing but wasted landscape that could have
been left wild or put to more productive uses, like growing food for
consumption by the land-user, which would free him up from having to work at
running some blasted machine to make money, to get in a car, to drive to the
supermarket, to buy the food, delivered and produced by a host of mechanical
devices, and futher separating the buyer from nature.
> larrry@my-dejanews.com wrote:
> >
> > Or at least I think he did.  Paved roads are the beginning of trouble,
I'll go
> > along with that, but one of the worst products of a technological society
is
> > the lawn and the lawnmower.  Where lawnmowers are needed, trouble is sure
to
> > follow.  Give me a place to live, on a dirt road, WHERE THERE ARE NO
> > LAWNMOWERS and I think I'll be about as near to heaven as I can get.
> >
> He did not:
>
>    48. It is well known that crowding increases stress and aggression.
>    The degree of crowding that exists today and the isolation of man
> from
>    nature are consequences of technological progress. All pre-industrial
>    societies were predominantly rural. The industrial Revolution vastly
>    increased the size of cities and the proportion of the population
> that
>    lives in them, and modern agricultural technology has made it
> possible
>    for the Earth to support a far denser population than it ever did
>    before. (Also, technology exacerbates the effects of crowding because
>    it puts increased disruptive powers in people's hands. For example, a
>    variety of noise-making devices: power mowers, radios, motorcycles,
>                                     ^^^^^ ^^^^^^
>    etc. If the use of these devices is unrestricted, people who want
>    peace and quiet are frustrated by the noise. If their use is
>    restricted, people who use the devices are frustrated by the
>    regulations... But if these machines had never been invented there
>    would have been no conflict and no frustration generated by them.)
>
> TK, ISAIF
>
